contentHtml:
The Micos Waterfalls (Cascadas de Micos) are a series of stepped waterfalls 20 minutes from Ciudad Valles, in the heart of the Huasteca Potosina, and they're considered one of the most complete adventure circuits in the state. Many travelers arrive with specific questions: How much is admission? Do I need a guide? Is there public transportation? Answering those questions before you go makes the difference between a day well spent and a wasted one. This guide to the Micos Waterfalls answers all of that with verified 2026 information.

Micos Waterfalls: quick facts

Admission$100 MXN per person; waterfall jumps, zip line, kayak and skybike are paid separately on site
HoursEvery day, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.
Getting thereIt's 20 minutes from Ciudad Valles. Combis (shared vans) leave every 30 minutes for about $35 MXN.
SafetyLife jacket and helmet required
Best time to goYear-round
TourParaíso Escalonado: from $1,600 MXN per person, 11 to 12 h, with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles; it adds the Minas Viejas Waterfalls the same day

In the sections below you'll find the full price breakdown, the activity options at Micos near Ciudad Valles, how to arrange transportation and what to bring to make the most of it.

What to see and do at the Micos Waterfalls, Ciudad Valles

What is the waterfall jumping circuit, and what does the local guide include?

The waterfall jumping circuit is the main activity here. Hiring a guide on site costs $180 MXN per person in 2026 and includes a life jacket, a helmet, the full route through all the waterfalls and GoPro photos sent to you on WhatsApp at the end. It usually starts around 9:00 a.m.

The travelers we coordinate through huasteca-potosina.com agree that having a local guide changes everything: guides know the safe jumping spots, the best photo angles and the timing to avoid crowds. If you want to add this to a bigger outing, book the Paraíso Escalonado tour ahead of time; it covers Micos and Minas Viejas in one day.

Skybike and zip lines: activities at a set price

The Skybike — a bicycle zip line over the river — costs $900 MXN and includes 3 zip lines and the suspension bridge. Additional activities range from $600 to $1,100 MXN, depending on the combination you choose. It's best to arrive early to get a spot on the most popular ones. The site is open every day from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. You can find more options when you see available tours in the Huasteca Potosina.

Activities and prices at Micos, Huasteca Potosina, in 2026

What groups experience on their first visit

Groups single out two moments: the first leap off the rocks and the walk across the suspension bridge. First-time visitors tend to underestimate how physical the circuit is; some stretches involve walking on wet rock and need your full attention. General admission costs $100 MXN per person and includes a life jacket from the entrance. In the rainy season — between June and September — the flow increases and some pools may close temporarily for safety.

Here's a summary of costs: general admission $100 MXN with life jacket included; guide for the jumping circuit an extra $180 MXN; Skybike with zip lines $900 MXN; extra activities from $600 to $1,100 MXN. For a full trip budget, read How much does it cost to visit the Huasteca Potosina in 2026?

Tips before visiting the Micos Waterfalls

  • Arrive before 9:00 a.m.: guided spots are limited on weekends, and arriving late can mean waiting or missing the photo session.
  • Plan your transportation ahead of time: it's 20 minutes from Ciudad Valles. Combis leave every 30 minutes for about $35 MXN. You can also reach Micos in the Huasteca Potosina in your own car, heading from Ciudad Valles toward El Naranjo. See your options in our 3-day Huasteca Potosina itinerary.
  • Know the best time of year: November to February brings cooler weather and smaller crowds. See the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina.
  • The right clothes and gear: wear water shoes or sandals with good grip, clothes that can get wet and water-resistant sunscreen. Don't bring valuables without a waterproof case.

Frequently asked questions about the Micos Waterfalls

How many waterfalls are there at Micos, near Ciudad Valles?

The site at Micos, Ciudad Valles has many stepped waterfalls that form natural pools along the river. The guided circuit covers all of them, with jumps, walking over rock and a swim in every pool.

How much is admission to the Micos Waterfalls in 2026?

General admission is $100 MXN per person and includes a life jacket. Hiring a guide for the jumping circuit costs an extra $180 MXN, with a helmet, the full route and GoPro photos. Extra activities such as the Skybike cost $900 MXN.

How do you get to the Micos Waterfalls from Ciudad Valles?

Here's how to get to the Micos Waterfalls: the site is 20 minutes from Ciudad Valles. Combis leave every 30 minutes for about $35 MXN. By car, head from Ciudad Valles toward El Naranjo.

Are the Micos Waterfalls safe for families with kids?

The site is family-friendly, although the jumps and the guided circuit are aimed at adults. For kids, the free-access pools and the suspension bridge are the best options. Children should wear a life jacket at all times. At Micos in the Huasteca Potosina, the life jacket is included with admission.
